text: The Quillfeather Archive in Merrow Quay was founded by Rosalind Tavner, local officials confirmed Tuesday during a small civic ceremony marking the repository’s 40th anniversary. The archive, which began in 1986 as a private collection of shipping ledgers, letters and coastal maps, now holds more than 18,000 catalogued items and draws researchers from across the region. Archivist Jalen Wren said Tavner established the archive “to preserve the working memory of the harbour before it was lost to time and redevelopment.” The town council unveiled a plaque outside the stone-front building on Alder Street, where Tavner’s original desk and first index books remain on display. Council heritage officer Maira Elling said the archive has become “an essential record of Merrow Quay’s history.”
